intervals.label: proposal
intervals.locator: CERN Courier, "The ring on the parking lot"
intervals.note: From 1964 to 1970 annual funding requests to the AEC were rejected (same article); the machine was then built from SLAC operating funds.
intervals.quote: first proposed building the Stanford Positron-Electron Asymmetric Rings (SPEAR) in 1964

intervals.label: construction
intervals.locator: CERN Courier, "The ring on the parking lot"
intervals.note: Funding agreed in 1970 (about 20 months before service in 1972); year precision.
intervals.quote: In 1972, only 20 months after its construction had finally been agreed, the SPEAR electron-positron collider went into service

intervals.label: e+e- collider operation
intervals.locator: SLAC Milestones; end from the 1990 entry
intervals.note: First physics data by spring 1973 (CERN Courier). From October 1979 half of SPEAR running time was dedicated to synchrotron radiation (Hallonsten); the end date is when SPEAR became a dedicated synchrotron-radiation facility.

intervals.label: dedicated synchrotron-radiation facility; collider operation ended
intervals.note: SPEAR has since run only as a synchrotron-radiation source (upgraded to SPEAR3 in 2004); photon science is outside the Atlas scope (A26), so this record covers the collider period only.
intervals.quote: 1990: SPEAR becomes a dedicated synchrotron radiation facility with its own independent injector.

name: Stanford Positron Electron Asymmetric Ring
notes: SSRL describes the tau as "discovered at SPEAR in 1976"; the discovery paper (Mark I, Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 1489) is dated December 1975, the date used on the result record.
The ring and its detectors are on the SLAC campus; the SPEAR site marker is the SLAC campus point, not the ring.

beam_energy.locator: SSRL, History of the SPEAR Storage Ring
beam_energy.quote: counter-rotating beams of electrons and positrons were circulated at energies up to 4 GeV

circumference.locator: Hallonsten, Physics in Perspective (SPEAR vs PEP circumference)
circumference.note: A historian's figure; SSRL describes the ring as "some 80 meters in diameter", which is roughly consistent (a ring of 80 m diameter would be about 250 m round).

cms_energy.locator: Perl Nobel lecture, "SPEAR and the Mark I Detector"
cms_energy.note: Perl adds that in the first few years the maximum energy with useful luminosity was 4.8 GeV.
cms_energy.quote: Eventually SPEAR obtained a total energy of about 8 GeV

summary.plain: SLAC's first electron-positron collider, a single ring about 80 metres across that began running in 1972. At SPEAR, the Mark I experiment found the J/psi particle (1974), proving the charm quark, and the tau lepton (1975). Since 1990 it has run only as an X-ray source.
summary.technical: SPEAR e⁺e⁻ storage ring at SLAC: beams up to 4 GeV (about 8 GeV total), 234 m circumference; operations began 1972; detectors Mark I (1973-1977), Mark II (1977-1979), Crystal Ball, Mark III (1981-1988); dedicated to synchrotron-radiation research from 1990 (now SPEAR3).
